title: The Quiet Inheritance
premise: Jonah Voss, a retired detective who quietly solved three deaths the police called accidents while running a failing bookshop, finds a drowned man on the riverbank wearing clothes stolen from her own closet. The victim is tied to the Harrow case — the drowning of her sister twenty-five years ago that everyone swore was closed for good, and that made Jonah quit the force. As the anniversary dinner of the founding families approaches, Jonah discovers the 'accident' was staged by someone still protecting the town's most beloved patriarch, and that the new victim had been blackmailing him with evidence he'd kept hidden for decades. In the end, Jonah exposes the killer at the anniversary dinner itself, chooses love over duty by shielding her estranged niece from prosecution as an accomplice, and finally claims her belonging in the town that spent a generation lying to her.
about_author: Oscar Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering coroner's inquests before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about places that keep their secrets politely.

chapters.title: Watermarks
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A quiet morning at the failing bookshop is broken when a jogger reports a body by the river. Jonah arrives first and recognizes the dead man's clothes: her own, taken from her closet. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coat
chapters.summary: Detective Mara Quist's POV. Quist, who owes Jonah for the three 'accidents' she quietly solved, notices the clothing detail but can't explain it. She reluctantly lets Jonah consult. Beat: uneasy alliance forming over professional pride.

chapters.title: Twenty-Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, flashback-woven. The victim is identified as Peter Lunn, a former police archivist. His name surfaces in the file of her sister Cass's drowning — the closed case that drove Jonah off the force. Beat: grief reopened like a wound.

chapters.title: The Anniversary List
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. The town prepares for the Founders' Dinner marking 25 years since the Harrow mill closing. Every guest list name overlaps with the old case file. Beat: creeping realization that the whole town is a suspect pool.

chapters.title: What the Bookshop Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Among Lunn's effects is a library slip for a book Jonah sold him months ago — inside it, a photocopy of a page torn from the original Harrow inquest. Beat: the past reaching through her own shelves.

chapters.title: Niece of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah's estranged niece Tessa arrives unannounced, asking to stay. Jonah learns Tessa was seen arguing with Lunn days before his death. Beat: love and suspicion tangled together.

chapters.title: The Patriarch's Smile
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. Edmund Harrow, the town's beloved elder statesman, gives a gracious interview about the anniversary. Quist notices his hands shake when Lunn's name comes up. Beat: charm as camouflage.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She revisits the three deaths she solved privately and realizes each victim had consulted Lunn shortly before dying. Lunn wasn't just an archivist — he was selling secrets. Beat: the pattern snapping into focus.

chapters.title: Closet Evidence
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. Forensics confirms the clothes were taken during a window when only a handful of people had access to Jonah's home above the shop. Beat: violation — the killer has been inside her life.

chapters.title: Tessa's Alibi
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Tessa produces an alibi that checks out, then confesses she'd been paid by Lunn to copy documents from Edmund Harrow's estate. Beat: betrayal and protectiveness colliding.

chapters.title: The Mill Pond File
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. The missing inquest page shows Cass's blood alcohol was falsified downward — someone doctored the report to close the case fast. Beat: righteous fury hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An anonymous note warns her to stop digging before the anniversary dinner. That night someone smashes the shop window and leaves a single wet shoe print matching her own stolen boots. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Edmund's Confessor
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. An elderly housekeeper reveals Lunn visited Harrow House monthly for years — always leaving with an envelope. Beat: the blackmail architecture exposed.

chapters.title: What Cass Saw
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Reconstructing her sister's last night, Jonah realizes Cass witnessed something at the mill pond the night Edmund's son died there decades earlier — the true origin of every secret since. Beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. The housekeeper is found dead in her bath, ruled accidental — but staged exactly like the old cases Jonah once unraveled. The killer is repeating history deliberately. Beat: escalation and horror.

chapters.title: A Message in Her Own Handwriting
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A forged suicide note in Jonah's handwriting appears, dated ahead of time — the killer plans to frame her for everything after the dinner. Beat: the trap closing around her.

chapters.title: Tessa Runs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tessa flees with the copied documents, forcing Jonah to choose between chasing her and meeting Quist. She lets Tessa go and trusts her niece's judgment. Beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: The Envelope's Contents
chapters.summary: Quist's POV. Tessa delivers the documents: proof Edmund's son killed a mill worker, that Cass saw it, and that Edmund arranged both cover-ups — including paying Lunn for silence ever since. Beat: the full truth assembled.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the Founders' Dinner, Jonah publicly confronts Edmund with the evidence as the town raises its toast. Edmund's son — now the respected sheriff's deputy — moves to silence her. Beat: climax, all masks off.

chapters.title: The Mill Pond Again
chapters.summary: Climax continues, Quist's POV. The deputy lures Jonah to the mill pond to stage her drowning, mirroring Cass. Quist and Tessa intervene; the deputy confesses in front of witnesses, and Edmund collapses under the weight of exposure. Beat: catharsis at the site of the original sin.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Official findings are rewritten; Jonah negotiates leniency for Tessa, choosing family over the letter of the law. She visits Cass's grave and reads the corrected report aloud. Beat: grief finally given its true shape.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue. Spring: the bookshop reopens with a new section on local history, honestly told. Tessa works the register; Quist brings cold cases instead of apologies. Beat: belonging earned, memory honored, love chosen.
